variant.stem_override: A 52-year-old Black or African American woman with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (anti-CCP 220 U/mL, RF 70 IU/mL) has been on methotrexate 25 mg subcutaneously weekly with folic acid for 6 months. She bridged off prednisone 3 months ago. Despite optimal MTX dosing and verified medication adherence, her DAS28 today is 3.8 (moderate disease activity, above the low-activity target of <3.2). Joint exam shows persistent synovitis of multiple MCP and wrist joints. ESR 45, CRP 18 mg/L. TB screening is NEGATIVE (negative tuberculin skin test and negative interferon-gamma release assay), hepatitis B and C are negative, HIV negative. She has no significant comorbidities and no current infections.

The correct answer (B) is unchanged because the treat-to-target escalation decision is driven entirely by DAS28, MTX optimization status, and TB screening results, none of which differ.
